title: First free locker number
prompt:
taken lists locker numbers already assigned, in any order and possibly with junk values; return the smallest positive integer that does not appear in taken.

- taken has 0 to 100,000 integers between -2^31 and 2^31 - 1; duplicates and non-positive values may appear.
- Target O(n) time and O(1) extra space. You may rearrange taken in place.
- Return a positive integer (1 if taken is empty).
hints: With n values, the answer is always between 1 and n + 1. Values outside that range cannot matter.
Use the array itself as the lookup table: try to place each value v in 1..n at index v - 1.
Swap taken[i] into slot taken[i] - 1 while it is in range and that slot does not already hold the same value. Then the first index i with taken[i] != i + 1 gives i + 1; if none, return n + 1.

solution.explanation: The answer lies in 1..n+1, so each in-range value v is swapped home to index v - 1 (cyclic placement). Every swap puts at least one value in its final slot, so there are at most n swaps in total. A second scan finds the first slot not holding its own number.

complexity.notes: The inner while loop does at most n swaps across the whole run because each swap fixes one value permanently. A hash set gives O(n) space without mutation.

followUps: Solve it in O(1) extra space without swapping, by marking presence with signs.
Return the k smallest missing positive integers instead of just the first.
